messages:
Ashley: noticing a spike of 429s from Dedicated pool `beta-3` — multiple customers reporting TPS SLO violations over the last hour
kevin: which error code? admission 429 or throttling 429? any auth errors too?
Ashley: admission 429 with reason `burst_credit_depleted` and a few long-tail latency reports (500s) around same time
sre-bot: alert: dedicated.pool.beta-3.tps_slo_violation count=18 since 2026-03-16T21:02Z
mari: can you paste a sample request/response and the exact timestamps? also which deploys happened recently to admission-controller?
Ashley: repro snippet from customer NEXA at 21:02UTC — they sent steady 450 tps with occasional spikes to 1k tps
Ashley: response headers: `x-redwood-error: admission_failed`, body: `{"reason":"burst_credit_depleted","pool":"beta-3"}`
oliver: checked deploys — admission-controller v2.1.4 rolled at 2026-03-16T20:50Z (rollout annotations: #PR-1249). That version included the new credit-decay optimization.
carla: trying a quick repro against beta-3 with a local load script
carla: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.test/dedicated/beta-3/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <tok>' -d '{"inputs":"x" * 128}' -w '\\n%{http_code} %{time_total}\\n' -o /dev/null
carla: got `429` consistently once sustained >600 tps for ~30s
mari: can you pull admission-controller logs around 20:55-21:05 for pool beta-3? look for `credit_update` and `credit_consumed` entries
carla: logs (grep):
```
2026-03-16T20:56:12Z admission: account=acme credit_consumed=1200 pool=beta-3
2026-03-16T20:56:12Z admission: account=acme credit_balance=0 pool=beta-3
2026-03-16T20:56:12Z admission: pool=beta-3 reason=burst_credit_depleted
2026-03-16T20:56:15Z admission: account=acme credit_update delta=-5 pool=beta-3
```
kevin: that `credit_update delta=-5` every 3s seems wrong — credits should decay at rate floor(allocated/60) not negative jitter like that
mari: agree, looks like the new decay math may underflow when allocation rounding happens. need to check PR-1249 changeset
billing-bot: note: customer NEXA has reserve credits configured: reserved_tokens_per_sec=800, burst_bucket=1200 (UI shows last sync 2026-03-16T18:00Z)
oliver: prom query to check served tokens by pool:
```
sum(rate(tokens_served_total{pool=\"beta-3\"}[1m])) by (pool)
```
oliver: graph shows spikes to ~1.1k tps at 20:55 and sustained 700-900 tps after
mari: also check `admission_burst_balance{pool=\"beta-3\"}` — we saw it drop to zero at the start of the spike
carla: dug into admission-controller code: new branch for credit decay used integer truncation, for small allocations it subtracts more than expected when rounding down — PR notes `allocation // 60` changed to `ceil(allocation / 60.0)` in later commit but we have older image
kevin: so beta-3 had a recent image with the buggy branch — did the rollout affect other pools? why only beta-3 impacted
mari: beta-3 is on Dedicated nodes with GPU type A100-small, drifted CPU utilization so autoscaler didn't spin extra nodes because admission-controller reported enough headroom (false positive)
Ashley: customers also reported longer queueing before 429s — admission controller was accepting but token consumption outpaced replenishment
oliver: suspect interplay between decayed credits and the admission window: if credits are undercounted we hit depletion faster and admission gating starts rejecting even though autoscaler could have added capacity
carla: temporary mitigation: increase `reserved_tokens_per_sec` for affected accounts to 1000 and bump `burst_bucket` to 1600 — that buys headroom until patch
Ashley: done for NEXA and 3 other impacted tenants — monitoring now
kevin: we should also consider a fail-open fallback: if admission-controller sees sustained queueing and cluster CPU headroom > 20% then let through until autoscaler reacts
mari: agreed but that's a product decision — create a proposal. For now we need an eng runtime hotfix to revert the decay change or apply ceil logic
carla: I can build a candidate image with the quick patch (PR-1256) that reverts to previous decay and adds unit tests for small allocations
oliver: schedule a canary on pool `gamma-1` (low-risk) and then roll to `beta-3` if green
sre-bot: action created: JIRA INF-3278 assigned to eng-runtime (priority P1) — link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3278
billing-bot: note: we saw billing meter `burst_credit_used` incremented heavily but no invoice discrepancy yet — keep billing in loop
Ashley: next steps: 1) patch release (carla) 2) canary (oliver) 3) config temporary increases applied (ashley) 4) postmortem template started (kevin)
kevin: please include exact PromQL queries, log excerpts, the offending image tag, and list of impacted accounts in the PM
carla: pushing image `admission-controller:v2.1.4-patch-1` now, will post canary results in ~15m
oliver: canary looks fine so far (gamma-1) — no 429s on the test harness
carla: rolling to `beta-3` in 2m
sre-bot: deploy-bot: rollout start admission-controller beta-3 -> image admission-controller:v2.1.4-patch-1 (canary passed)
Ashley: after roll to beta-3 — credits stabilized and 429s stopped within 90s. customers report latency normalized
kevin: follow-up: schedule regression test in CI for credit math, and add alert on `admission_burst_balance` depletion rate > threshold to trigger earlier mitigation
mari: assigning PM/Owner: eng-runtime (oliver), SRE follow-up (kevin)
Ashley: leaving notes in customer tickets and closing the urgent channel once PM confirms postmortem
carla: linking PR here: https://github.com/redwood/admission/pull/1256
kevin: thanks all — great triage. :thumbsup:
